'''Roger Arthur Cowley''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]],<ref name=rsbm/> [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh|FRSE]], [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics|FInstP]] (24 February 1939 – 27 January 2015) was an English [[physicist]] who specialised in the excitations of [[solids]].<ref name=ox/> 

==Biography==
Cowley was born in [[Woodford Green]], Essex, on 24 February 1939. His father, Cecil Arthur Cowley, was a chartered surveyor, and his mother Mildred Sarah Nash was from a farming family. During [[World War II]], the family evacuated to [[Leighton Buzzard]], [[Bedfordshire]], later moving to [[Shenfield]] and on to [[Gidea Park]], Essex.  He was educated at [[Brentwood School, Essex|Brentwood School]], where he had won a scholarship, and afterwards he entered [[Trinity Hall, Cambridge]], where he read [[natural sciences]]. Cowley would remain at Cambridge to study for a PhD.<ref name="ODNB">{{cite journal |last1=Birgeneau |first1=Robert J. |title=Cowley, Roger Arthur (1939–2015) |journal=Oxford Dictionary of National Biography |date=10 January 2019|doi=10.1093/odnb/9780198614128.013.110390 }}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=The lattice dynamics of ionic crystals|first= Roger Arthur|last=Cowley|date=1964|url=https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.598091|website=ethos.bl.uk|oclc=879394371}}</ref> 

He married Sheila Joyce Wells, a teacher of mathematics, on 4 April 1964 and they had two children. On 27 January 2015 Cowley died at a care home in Oxford as a result of a head injury sustained in a bicycle accident a year earlier.<ref name=ODNB/>

==Career and research==
He was appointed professor of physics at the [[University of Edinburgh]] in 1970 and [[Dr Lee's Professor of Experimental Philosophy]] at the [[University of Oxford]] in 1988 (a post that carried with it a [[fellow]]ship at [[Wadham College, Oxford]]).<ref name=ox>{{cite web|url=http://xray.physics.ox.ac.uk/Cowley/CV_Roger.htm|title=Roger Cowley CV|website=physics.ox.ac.uk|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716144536/http://xray.physics.ox.ac.uk/Cowley/CV_Roger.htm|archivedate=16 July 2011|first=Roger|last=Cowley|year=2011|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Cowley made his name in the field of [[neutron scattering]]. This work led to the study of [[phase transition]]s.<ref name=ODNB/>

==Awards and honours==
In 1972 Cowley was elected a fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh and the following year he was awarded the inaugural [[Max Born Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540891.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-12101|title=Cowley, Prof. Roger Arthur, (24 Feb. 1939 - 27 Jan. 2015), Dr Lee's Professor of Experimental Philosophy, University of Oxford,1988 - 2007, then Emeritus Professor of Physics; Fellow of Wadham College, Oxford, 1988 - 2007, then Emeritus {{!}} WHO'S WHO & WHO WAS WHO|website=www.ukwhoswho.com|language=en|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.u12101|isbn=978-0-19-954089-1 |access-date=2019-01-27}}</ref> He was elected [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1978|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1978]]<ref name=rsbm/> and awarded the [[Fernand Holweck Medal and Prize]] in 1990.<ref name=ODNB/> In 2003 he received the Walter Hälg Prize from the European Neutron Scattering Association and the [[Institute of Physics Michael Faraday Medal and Prize|Faraday Medal and Prize]] from the [[Institute of Physics]] in 2008.<ref name=rsbm/>
